identity.name: Phrygia
alt_names: Mushki (Assyrian name, identified with the Phrygians by most historians for Midas's time)

land.text: the Phrygian highlands, which Lydia 'extended over' after expelling the Cimmerians by around 620 BC, and the Troad taken by Gyges after Phrygia's collapse

successors.note: No state held the land between the Cimmerian sack of Gordion (676) and the Lydian advance (c. 620); the Phrygia infobox lists the Cimmerians and Lydia as successors.

capitals.name: Gordion (Gordium)
capitals.note: Infobox 'Capital: Gordion'. Coordinates are the gazetteer's Gordion. The page gives no earlier or later capital; Gordium was violently destroyed c. 675 BC (excavations).

keyframe_review.note: 29,488 km2 around Gordion, -900..-751. The Phrygia page gives no infobox area and no extent for these centuries, and no ruler or event before Midas (740-675 in the infobox); the shape cannot be checked against a figure and is kept as Cliopatria's (unverified: page budget).

78,628 km2 (30.5-34.75 E, 38.5-42.0 N), -750..-701. The Midas page has Midas (Mita of the Mushki) attacking Assyria's eastern Anatolian provinces under Sargon II; the Tabal page has him press Ambaris of Tabal from c. 714. Neither gives a Phrygian border; the shape's reach to the Black Sea coast (42.0 N) and to the Halys bend (34.75 E, overlapping Tabal's west edge at 34.5 E) is unverified. The Great Tumulus at Gordion, timbers c. 740, is now thought to cover Midas's father (Midas page). No infobox area.

correction.text: Phrygia's -700 shape without the Lydian kingdom of Gyges around Sardis; Gyges took the Troad with little resistance after Phrygia's collapse (Gyges page, paraphrase).

keyframe_review.note: 188,102 km2 (26.7-35.2 E, 37.2-42.0 N), -700..-676: Cliopatria draws Phrygia across all of western Anatolia to the Aegean, on top of its own Lydia shape (-700..-676, 24,042 km2 around Sardis). Gyges of Lydia reigned at Sardis in these years (c. 717-679 or c. 680-644) and took the Troad after Phrygia's collapse (Gyges page, paraphrase), so the Lydian core is removed. The Phrygia page gives no extent for the west; the rest of the shape (Troad, Aegean coast) is unverified and may be too generous.

region.text: the Phrygian core around Gordion (Cliopatria -900 shape, 29,488 km2)

ledger.note: 900 (page silent): Phrygia at Gordion. The Phrygia page gives no founding year; its infobox lists the Bryges, Mushki and Hittites as predecessors with 'Bronze Age Collapse: 1200 BC'. -900 is Cliopatria's first Phrygia shape, around the capital Gordion.

region.text: the Assyrian provinces in eastern Anatolia and Tabal, where Midas pressed Ambaris from c. 714

ledger.note: 715: Phrygia and Assyria come to blows. 'Phrygia engaged in military conflict with Assyria from 715 BC' (Phrygia page); the Midas page has Mita of the Mushki attack Assyria's eastern Anatolian provinces in Sargon's reign, and the Tabal page has Midas press Ambaris of Tabal (Bit-Burutash) from c. 714 until Sargon annexed it in 713. The page gives no front; Cappadocia and Tabal are the researcher's reading.

region.text: the Assyrian-Phrygian front in Cappadocia and Tabal

ledger.note: 709: Phrygia submits and a truce is struck. An inscription of 709 BC under Sargon 'suggests' that Phrygia 'had offered its submission and struck a truce by that time' (Phrygia page); 'the Assyrians incorporated some hitherto eastern Phrygian territory' (undated).

region.text: the Phrygian kingdom, left to the Cimmerian raiders

ledger.note: 676: the Cimmerians destroy Gordion. The Phrygia lead says they 'sacked the Phrygian capital, Gordium, around 695 BC' while excavations 'confirm a violent destruction of Gordium around 675 BC' (infobox 'Fall to the Cimmerians: 675 BC'); the Midas page gives Midas's suicide as c. 695 (Eusebius) or c. 676 (Julius Africanus). Cliopatria's Phrygia row ends in -676. The land passed to no state until Lydia took it c. 620 (lydia dossier) and Gyges took the Troad (Gyges page).

676: Phrygia ends. Midas is 'the last independent king of Phrygia' before the Cimmerian sack (Phrygia page); dates for the fall range from c. 695 to 675 BC across the page and the Midas page, and -676 (Africanus) is Cliopatria's last year.

wars.name: Phrygian-Assyrian conflict
wars.outcome: A truce and Phrygian submission by 709 under Sargon II; some eastern Phrygian land was later incorporated by the Assyrians.
wars.note: Midas (Mita of the Mushki) pressed Ambaris of Tabal from c. 714 (Tabal page); Sargon II annexed Tabal in 713.

wars.name: Cimmerian sack of Gordion
wars.outcome: Gordium sacked and burned; Midas dies; the kingdom does not recover.
wars.note: 695 (lead, Eusebius), 676 (Julius Africanus) or 675 (excavation, infobox) BC; the Gyges page says c. 675.

certainty.note: No page opened gives a Phrygian border; the whole life is soft.

sources.title: Phrygia
sources.note: State article: capital Gordion, Cimmerian sack 695/675, Assyria from 715, 709 truce, Lydian takeover; no infobox area.

sources.title: Midas
sources.note: Midas as Mita of the Mushki, Sargon II, death c. 695 or 676, Gordium destroyed.

sources.title: Tabal (state)
sources.note: Midas presses Ambaris c. 714; Tabal annexed 713; opened for the tabal-kingdom dossier and used here.

sources.title: Gyges of Lydia
sources.note: Phrygia destroyed c. 675; the Troad after Phrygia's collapse; Gyges at Sardis; opened for the lydia dossier and used here.

notes:
Page budget 1-2 pages: the Phrygia and Midas pages were opened for this state; the Tabal and Gyges pages belong to the tabal-kingdom and lydia dossiers and are cited where they carry a Phrygian fact. No infobox area exists on the Phrygia page, so the three Cliopatria areas (29k, 79k, 188k km2) are unchecked.

Open points: (1) The -700 shape reaches the Aegean and overlaps Cliopatria's own Lydia shape; the pages give no Phrygian border in the west, so only the Lydian core is removed. A gap-filler should read the Seshat page (tr_phrygian_k) for the extent. (2) The Midas page says the Assyrian texts' Mita of the Mushki is 'the same person' only per 'most historians'; Phrygian-Mushki identity is not settled. (3) The fall is dated 695 (Eusebius, the lead), 676 (Africanus) or 675 (excavations, infobox); -676 is kept for Cliopatria's row. (4) The 709 truce is read as submission by the page ('suggests'); the Neo-Assyrian dossier should decide whether to carry a vassal_start for Phrygia. (5) Phrygia's Cliopatria neighbours were greek-city-states, lydia and neo-assyrian-empire in -700..-676; the Greek cities are not mentioned on the pages opened. (6) Midas's reign is 740-675 in the infobox and c. 720-c. 695/676 in the body; no ruler strip is given.
